en.title: Longest No-Backtracking Route Through a Cave
en.description:
Start from the top-left corner (0,0) of the grid and reach the bottom-right corner. ! is a passable cell and x is an obstacle. Each step moves exactly one cell left, right, or down; you cannot move up or re-enter a visited cell. Find the maximum number of cells on a path that reaches the exit (counting both the start and the end); output −1 if the exit cannot be reached.

The standard input, this site's constraints, the examples, and the test data were independently compiled by CSWork.
en.input: This site's input: the first line contains R C (1..200), followed by R strings of length C containing only ! and x; the entrance or exit may also be blocked.
en.output: Output the maximum number of visited cells, or −1.
en.explanation:
Example 1: in an empty 3×3 grid you can snake row by row through all 9 cells and finish at the bottom-right corner.

Example 2: the cells to the right of and below the entrance are both obstacles, so the exit cannot be reached; the output is −1.

Example 3: the start is also the end and is passable, so the number of visited cells is 1.
hints: Use row-by-row dynamic programming. Each row is entered by descending from the previous row; do one left-to-right scan and one right-to-left scan, take the larger value at each position, and use it as the entry for the next row.
